textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 english · The Big Laddoo · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: The poem plays with one idea again and again: what if many small things became one very big thing. It talks about laddoos, children and seas. In each case, many small ones join to make one big one.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A laddoo is round, and many things around us are round, such as a ball, a coin, an orange, a wheel and the moon. Some round things can be eaten, like an orange or a laddoo. Some cannot be eaten, like a ball or a wheel.

textbookBox.concept: In some words two consonant sounds come together at the start. Both sounds are still there when we say the blend. Pl words are play, plum, plate and plant. Cl words are cloud, clock, clap and clean.

beats.en: Many animals have a male name and a female name. A cock is a male bird and a hen is the female. A lion is male and a lioness is female. A peacock is male and a peahen is female. A mare is a female horse.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 english · The Big Laddoo · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: Some things float on water and some things sink. A dry leaf or feather laid gently on water often stays on the surface. A small piece of dry paper can float at first and may sink after it gets wet.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from The Big Laddoo: Some things float on water and some things sink. A dry leaf or feather laid gently on water often stays on the surface. A small piece of dry paper can float at first and may sink after it gets wet.
